feature: Accepted captured widths versus historical confirmation tests
synopsis: 494 tests across91 suites executed; two historical tests failed at four assertions after accepted scan dimensions changed. All observed failures demand that usable high-confidence captured widths remain unconfirmed, conflicting with the new accepted-dimensions requirement.

failures.diagnosis: After separately confirming actual exterior relation, operability, step-free status and grade, the test still expects a width-confirmation warning and wheelchair no-route solely because width came from scan. Accepted captured width now removes that artificial blocker.
failures.fix: Assert high/medium valid recorded scan width is usable without manual confirmation; retain positive width-clearance geometry checks and distinct unknown exterior/operability/grade safeguards. Add a low-confidence/invalid-width case that remains unknown and cannot authorize wheelchair clearance.

failures.diagnosis: The test globally asserts no imported width is confirmed even for its high-confidence surfaces.
failures.fix: Separate geometry acceptance from safety-role verification: assert valid width accepted while portals remain proposed, no exterior designation inferred, operability unknown and no route before those independent facts are supported. Keep wall-only irregular outline/measurement uncertainty checks where genuinely applicable.

recommendations: Rename blanket never-verified-anything wording so it distinguishes measurement evidence from exit/route/operability certification.
Do not revert accepted captured dimensions to satisfy obsolete manual-width confirmation assertions. Keep low-confidence, zero/invalid dimension, inaccessible-width and unknown-safety regressions.
Re-run full Core after expectations plus meaningful uncertainty cases are reconciled; observed failures alone do not prove every new accepted-width case correct.
limitations: Source and failed deterministic tests only; actual RoomPlan hardware measurement accuracy and native Save remain unverified.
Four failed assertions occur in two test methods, not four independent product defects.
